rows.grounds: compound of brahma, jñāna, and maya; describes the nature of the supreme reality
compound of brahma, ānanda, and maya; parallel attribute of the supreme reality
indeclinable indicating continuation or parallel quality

items.question: What forms of knowledge and bliss constitute the supreme Brahman addressed to the goddess?
premises: The supreme Brahman is described as consisting of Brahman-knowledge.
The supreme Brahman is likewise described as consisting of Brahman-bliss.
These attributes are declared directly to the goddess.
items.inference: The supreme Brahman is essentially constituted of both Brahman-knowledge and Brahman-bliss.
uncertainties: The grammatical case of the -maya compounds is taken as neuter nominative singular in apposition with the previously described supreme Brahman.
items.plain_english: O goddess, it is likewise consisting of the knowledge of Brahman and the bliss of Brahman.
